holidays.name: National Cheese Doodle Day
holidays.description: A day for crunchy, puffy, fingertip-staining orange snacks. Break out a bag of cheese doodles, and don't bother with a napkin. The orange dust is part of the fun.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that fans of cheesy snacks have celebrated for years. Its founder is unclear. Cheese puffs themselves became a mid-20th-century American snack craze after cornmeal extrusion made the light, crunchy texture possible.
holidays.funFact: Cheese doodles are made by pushing cornmeal dough through an extruder. It puffs up as it hits the air, and the puffs are then dusted with cheese powder. That's why they melt in your mouth.

holidays.name: Cinco de Marcho
holidays.description: A pun on Cinco de Mayo that gives March 5 its own party. Anyone can join in with a themed snack, a goofy toast, or a taco-shaped excuse to celebrate the arrival of spring.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It grew out of wordplay: swap the 'y' in 'Mayo' for an 'h' and you get the March version.
holidays.funFact: 'Cinco' means 'five' in Spanish. The pun works because March 5 is the fifth day of the third month, just as Cinco de Mayo falls on the fifth day of May.

holidays.name: Learn What Your Name Means Day
holidays.description: A day to look up the meaning and history behind your first name, and maybe your last name too. You might find out you're named for a warrior, a flower, or a medieval job.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's popular with genealogy fans and the baby-name-curious.
holidays.funFact: Many surnames started as occupations. Smith, Miller, and Cooper all point to a trade an ancestor once practiced.
